title: kate-ui: show the find bar
summary: cmd-f opens a find bar under the tab bar and focuses its field. Enter finds the next hit and shift-enter the previous one; cmd-g and cmd-shift-g do the same from the editor. cmd-alt-f opens the replace field. Toggles for regex, case, and whole word sit in the bar. Hits are painted behind the text.

lane.reason: A Cursor local agent on the owner Mac codes this packet. session.rs imports GPUI, the crate builds only on macOS, and the owner looks at the window after the change.

definitions.definition:
/// Map a key name in the find field to its action name, or None for text input.
fn find_field_action(binding: &str) -> Option<&'static str>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Store a findbar::FindState on WindowRoot. ShowFind sets open and moves focus to the field; typing edits bar.pattern and runs find_command from the primary caret on each change; CloseFind (escape) closes and returns focus to the editor. FindNext and FindPrevious set bar.backwards and run find_command; ReplaceOne runs replace_one_command for the current hit then FindNext; ReplaceAll runs replace_all_command. The toggles flip bar.mode between Plain and Regex, bar.case_sensitive, and bar.whole_words. Bind cmd-f, cmd-alt-f, cmd-g, cmd-shift-g, cmd-alt-r, cmd-alt-c, cmd-alt-w, and escape while the bar has focus. paint::hit_spans turns FindBar::highlights into column spans per line and the line paint fills them with a lighter selection color before the text. find_field_action maps enter to FindNext, shift-enter to FindPrevious, escape to CloseFind, and other names to None. The test find_field_action_names_the_keys asserts those three and that a is None. The owner types a word, sees the hits, and replaces one. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.
